canonical_name: Event-stream maintainer succession and the 2018 Copay supply-chain incident

stressor.event_description: npm describes an attacker posing as a maintainer taking over event-stream. The new maintainer added flatmap-stream as a dependency on September 9, 2018.

intervention.mechanism: On November 26, 2018, npm removed flatmap-stream and event-stream 3.3.6 and took ownership of event-stream.

perspectives.formal_charter: No project-specific succession charter is established by the cited reports. Registry ownership and package removal were available administrative powers.
perspectives.post_mortem_consensus: npm and BitPay identify a dependency-mediated attack on Copay. Analyst interpretation: delegated release authority created downstream exposure. This is a single-coder synthesis, not evidence of universal consensus.

structural_divergences.historical_analog: An indiscriminate malicious dependency affecting every consumer
structural_divergences.divergence_rationale: npm reports environment-specific targeting of Copay; broad dependency reach alone therefore does not measure the number of affected users.

evidence_sources.title: How BitPay is Securing the Copay and BitPay Wallets: NPM and Networking Security Updates for v5.3.1

telemetry.t_immediate: 2018-11-26: npm reports package removal and registry ownership intervention (npmIncidentReport).
telemetry.t_stabilized: By 2018-12-12: BitPay reports a Copay fix and added safeguards; stabilization and user recovery were not independently measured (bitpayResponse).
telemetry.t_terminal: Unknown: no terminal outcome or long-run follow-up was collected.

review_status: AI-authored example; no independent human review documented
